title: Injectivity modulo the maximal ideal into a flat module (Noetherian local)
statement: Let $\varphi:(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak m_S)$ be a local homomorphism of local rings (commutative rings with exactly one maximal ideal; $\varphi(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$) with $S$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $M$ be an $R$-module which is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], let $N$ be a finite $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], regarded as an $R$-module via $\varphi$, and let $u:N\to M$ be an $R$-linear map. If the induced map $\bar u:N/\mathfrak mN\to M/\mathfrak mM$ is injective, then $u$ is injective and the $R$-module $M/u(N)$ is flat.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00ME (lemma-mod-injective, line 23424), proof lines 23436-23477 (Krull intersection theorem, Lemma lemma-intersect-powers-ideal-module-zero; flatness via Tor, Lemma lemma-characterize-flat). Tag verified in tags/tags: 00ME,algebra-lemma-mod-injective

proof.text: Put $u_n:N/\mathfrak m^nN\to M/\mathfrak m^nM$. The hypothesis is injectivity of $u_1$. For $n\ge1$ put $Q_n=\mathfrak m^n/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$. Right exactness gives $N\otimes_R Q_n\to N/\mathfrak m^{n+1}N\to N/\mathfrak m^nN\to0$; flatness of $M$ makes the analogous sequence for $M$ exact also at the left. The first arrows are induced by multiplication, and the identifications $N\otimes_RQ_n\cong(N/\mathfrak mN)\otimes_{R/\mathfrak m}Q_n$ and $M\otimes_RQ_n\cong(M/\mathfrak mM)\otimes_{R/\mathfrak m}Q_n$ respect $u$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00ME (lemma-mod-injective), first paragraph, lines 23436-23454

proof.text: Assume $u_n$ injective. Since $R/\mathfrak m$ is a field, tensoring the injective $u_1$ with the $R/\mathfrak m$-vector space $Q_n$ is injective. In the diagram of the sequences from the preceding step, if a class $x\in N/\mathfrak m^{n+1}N$ maps to zero under $u_{n+1}$, its image under $u_n$ is zero, so $x$ comes from $N\otimes_RQ_n$. Its image in $M\otimes_RQ_n$ is zero because the lower first arrow is injective; the left vertical map is injective, hence $x=0$. Thus induction gives injectivity of $u_n$ for every $n\ge1$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00ME (lemma-mod-injective), first paragraph, lines 23436-23454

proof.text: The ideal $\mathfrak mS$ lies in the unique maximal ideal of $S$. Since $S$ is Noetherian and $N$ finite over $S$, Krull intersection gives $\bigcap_{n\ge1}(\mathfrak mS)^nN=0$. As $(\mathfrak mS)^nN=\mathfrak m^nN$, an element of $\ker u$ belongs to every $\mathfrak m^nN$ by injectivity of $u_n$, and therefore is zero.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00ME (lemma-mod-injective), second paragraph, lines 23456-23462; Krull intersection Tag 00IP

proof.text: Let $C=M/u(N)$ and let $I\subseteq R$ be any ideal. From $0\to N\xrightarrow{u}M\to C\to0$, the first-variable Tor exact sequence and flatness of $M$ identify $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(C,R/I)$ with the kernel of $N\otimes_RR/I\to M\otimes_RR/I$, hence with the kernel of $N/IN\to M/IM$. The flatness-Tor criterion reduces the conclusion to injectivity of these maps for all $I$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00ME (lemma-mod-injective), third paragraph, lines 23464-23473; Tor criterion Tag 00M5 and exact sequence Tag 00M0

proof.text: If $I=R$, then $N/IN=M/IM=0$. Otherwise $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, so $IS\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$. The induced map $R/I\to S/IS$ is local, $S/IS$ is Noetherian (each ascending chain of its ideals lifts to one in $S$), and $N/IN$ is finite over $S/IS$. The $R/I$-module $M/IM$ is flat, and reduction of $N/IN\to M/IM$ modulo $\mathfrak m/I$ is exactly $u_1$, hence injective. Apply the injectivity argument of steps 1-3, with $R/I,S/IS,N/IN,M/IM$ in place of $R,S,N,M$, to obtain injectivity for this $I$. Step 4 now gives flatness of $C$.
